items.title: expo/skills
items.content:
A collection of AI agent skills for working with Expo projects and Expo Application Services

Official AI agent skills from the Expo team for building, deploying, upgrading, and debugging Expo apps.

Skills give AI agents focused Expo knowledge: when to use Expo APIs, how to structure common workflows, and which Expo, EAS, React Native, iOS, and Android constraints matter. Expo documentation, Expo CLI, and EAS CLI remain the source of truth; these skills help agents apply them correctly.

For Claude Code or Codex, install the plugin so updates are handled by the official plugin marketplace. For Cursor, OpenCode, and other AI coding agents, use the skills CLI.

Claude Code or Codex, with updates handled by their official plugin marketplaces.
Cursor, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Gemini, Cline, AMP, Factory Droid, Antigravity, Kiro CLI, and other AI coding agents.
npx skills@latest add expo/skills --skill '*'

This selects every Expo skill without selecting every agent. The CLI will still ask where to install them; to target one agent directly, add .

For most agents, this is the only install command you need. Run it from the project root, then restart or refresh your agent session so it can discover the installed files.

Install from the official Claude Code plugin marketplace:

claude plugin install expo@claude-plugins-official

You can also run /plugin install expo@claude-plugins-official inside Claude Code.

Install from the OpenAI-curated Codex marketplace:

codex plugin add expo@openai-curated

You can also open in Codex and install from the OpenAI-curated marketplace.

Claude Code and Codex plugin installs are updated through their official plugin marketplaces.

For skills CLI installs, update installed skills with:

To update a single Expo skill, pass its name:

npx skills@latest update expo-router

After installing, ask your agent Expo-specific questions like:

  • "Build a native-feeling Expo Router screen with tabs, modals, and animations."
  • "Create an EAS workflow that builds previews on pull requests."
  • "Help me upgrade this app to the latest Expo SDK."
  • "Check whether this EAS Update rollout is healthy."

Agents choose the right skill from the task context and each skill's description.

Skills come in two groups so the free vs paid boundary is clear. Each skill's description carries the same label, and every services skill opens with a costs/plan-limits note.

Load this first for any Expo/EAS task, then route to the specific skill below.

Router and shared setup rules; the entry point when a request is vague or the user hasn't named a specific Expo tool.

Free, open-source Expo SDK and React Native skills.

Folder structure for a new Expo app: layout, routes-only , screens, server code, platform-specific files.
Expo Router navigation: file-based routes, links, native stacks, modals, sheets, native tabs, and headers.
Polished React Native animations and gestures with Reanimated, Gesture Handler, Expo Router, and expo-haptics.
Native-feeling screen styling, semantic colors, controls, icons, media, and visual effects.
In-app design systems: a token theme (color, spacing, typography, radius, shadow, motion), reusable component conventions, and design-system drift audits.
native components: universal cross-platform first, with SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose for platform-specific needs.
API calls, React Query, SWR, caching, offline support, and Expo Router data loaders.
Expo DOM components for gradually using web code in native apps.
Migrating an existing web/React app (Next.js, Vite, CRA) to a native iOS/Android app with Expo.
Expo native modules and views with Swift, Kotlin, TypeScript, config plugins, and autolinking.
Adding Expo or React Native to an existing iOS or Android app.
Development clients (local builds are free; EAS Build/TestFlight is a paid step).
The repo of integrations to adapt or scaffold a new project from.
iOS App Clip targets, AASA files, associated domains, and Smart App Banners.
Expo SDK upgrades, dependency conflicts, deprecated packages, and cache cleanup.

Services & paid distribution

Skills whose core purpose uses paid Expo Application Services (EAS).

Build and submit iOS/Android apps: Expo and other React Native projects, plus existing native apps; TestFlight, profiles, versioning, and metadata.
Deploying Expo websites and Expo Router API routes to EAS Hosting: secrets, custom domains, Cloudflare Workers.
EAS Workflow YAML files and CI/CD automation.
EAS Observe setup and launch, route, event, and version metrics.
EAS Update setup, OTA publishing, runtime compatibility, testing, and debugging.
EAS Update health, crash rates, launch counts, payload size, and rollout gates.
Run and drive your app on a remote iOS simulator or Android emulator on EAS cloud - from the CLI or an agent, with a live browser preview (iOS only).

Skills for Expo APIs that are not finalized. Content may change or be retired; skills graduate to the groups above when the underlying API stabilizes. These ship in the separate plugin (install it alongside ), or individually via the skills CLI.

Migrating a Swift Expo module from the Modules API 1.0 definition DSL to the 2.0 macro API.

Skills teach an agent how Expo work gets done. The Expo MCP server gives it live access to actually do that work: read the latest Expo docs on demand, install compatible dependencies with , trigger and monitor EAS builds and workflows, pull crash data from TestFlight, and screenshot a running app in the simulator.

The plugin bundles this MCP configuration, so Claude Code and Codex plugin installs wire it up automatically. For other agents, or to add it on its own, follow the Expo MCP setup guide.

Which AI coding agents are supported?

Use npx skills@latest add expo/skills --skill '*' for Cursor, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Gemini, Cline, AMP, Factory Droid, Antigravity, Kiro CLI, and similar AI coding tools.

Should I install the skills or the plugin?

Use the plugin for Claude Code or Codex; it stays updated through the plugin marketplace. Use npx skills@latest add expo/skills --skill '*' for Cursor, OpenCode, and other AI coding agents.

What is the source of truth?

Expo documentation, Expo CLI, and EAS CLI are the source of truth. These skills teach agents how to apply Expo guidance in real projects.

Every skill includes instructions to submit specific, actionable feedback with npx --yes @expo/agent-cli@latest feedback.

items.title: macro-inc/macro
items.content:
Macro is a unified workspace for teams: email, chat, docs, tasks, agents, calls, and CRM — @-linked together with shared AI memory.

Macro is the all-in-one workspace for you and your team. It unifies email + messages + docs + tasks + agents + CRM into a single fast interface with shared team-level memory. Everything in your workspace is @linked and searchable so your team (and your agents) never have to switch tools.

We built Macro because we wanted a single operating system for our startup. There are many good software products, and we used them all — Slack, Linear, Notion, HubSpot, and Superhuman — but they don't work together as one system. As we scaled our last venture to ~20 people things started to break: every team got their own tools and the company was held together by MCP and Zapier. The company was not computable. It was chaotic.

Macro is a complete redesign of work software from the ground up as a single system.

Designed by us in NYC and Toronto, dogfooded by our team of ~15 for two years. Built in SolidJS and Rust for speed and reliability. We're focused on building something that any small company or team at a larger company can use as their "operating system".

Macro is composed of 'blocks' designed to be modular, extensible, and work together like Lego. For each block, we studied the best prior art and tried to make it even better.

Each surface is purpose-built for its job rather than composed from a generic block primitive — but every one of them shares the same backend; cross-references between a doc and a task, or a channel message and an email, are natively stored as a .

Multi-account unified inbox, keyboard shortcuts, and shared inboxes. Gmail.
Channels and direct messages designed for focused technical discussions.
Linear-inspired tasks, tightly integrated with channels, email, and agents.
Real-time collaborative, markdown-native docs built on CRDTs, with @mentions.
2D board with embedded @links to tasks, files, and emails.
Unified, team-level memory. Can take action on your behalf.
Recorded, transcribed, and logged to team memory for agents.
Auto-imported from email and channels, fully searchable.
Linked to tasks, embeddable in channels, available to agents.
Customer and contact objects, custom properties, email sync, enrichment.

Macro Mail is inspired by Superhuman's keyboard-first interface with a few key additions:

  1. Multi-account. Triage all your Google accounts in a single inbox, with the same tagging and sharing system. Or triage individually.
  2. Unified inbox: emails, messages, @mentions, and tasks to complete, all in the same list. Use and to navigate everything.
  3. Better AI, with a tools/MCP surface designed to work across inboxes and to help your agents more accurately retrieve information. For example, we expose a unified search tool that allows agents to search all file attachment PDFs (parsed out of email) directly, rather than pulling email threads then attachments. You can also draft, edit and send emails right from AI chats, without opening your email.
  1. Multitasking ability — Macro has a built-in window manager that lets you create 3+ splits (scales with monitor size) so you can draft emails while reviewing prior threads.
  2. Company/Contact objects. Macro has native CRM capability so you can to a contact, like tim@acme.com to see all emails between you and that person, or companies, to see all emails and files between everyone on your team and everyone at that company, e.g. . All of this right from your email without having to open a heavyweight CRM like HubSpot or Salesforce. Email aggregation by contact or company is also available to your agents so they can better assist with CRM-type queries and actions.

Macro Mail lives in the same interface as channels, docs, tasks, and code. From any email, hit "task" to create a linked task, e.g. a ticket for an engineer from a customer support email. @mention emails in documents, e.g. @Re: Contract Signature.eml inside of Todos.md. In Macro, your email is brought into the fold with all of your tools, and your team, in the same permissions system: just hit to share an email to any DM or channel — no need to screenshot.

Macro Chat is designed to be more focused than Slack. The first couple of replies show inline and the rest collapse into a thread, so a busy channel stays readable. Threads are permissioned severally so you can share threads across channels by copying links. Everything is stored in a bidirectional graph, so tasks @link to messages that created them, customer support emails tie into support channels, CRM records get updated when they're discussed in messages, etc. The core idea is that (i) messaging should be the centerpiece around which tasks, mail, docs, and content management are built, all in a lightweight way, and agents should be first-class citizens like human users and (ii) messaging needs to be more focused and readable for technical conversations, and not turn into battles where context is lost and progress is indistinguishable from noise.

Linear recently published a report that issue tracking is dead. We agree with that, but the stronger form is that issue tracking never really worked, at least for us. We really tried and we blamed ourselves, but as we talked to other companies, it turns out that nobody was using their issue tracker "correctly". And if that's the case, the problem is the design of the tool, not the companies that use it.

The core problem with traditional issue trackers or project management tools is that they get out of date. The reason they get out of date is that (i) they're a separate system from where the conversation really happens in team chat (e.g. Slack, Macro, Discord, etc.) and (ii) they don't add much benefit beyond tracking the work. They're a chore with near-term costs and only the promise of long-term benefit. They're too rigid compared to a 2D canvas, too opinionated, and don't match how your project actually functions.

The solution isn't to forgo tracking entirely. We tried that and it was a different form of chaos. The solution we've found is lightweight issues tightly coupled to your channels and DMs, so that issue tracking naturally occurs where the conversation itself happens.

Creating tasks in Macro is easy. Where possible, tasks created are bidirectionally linked to the creating context (e.g. a customer email) so the full chain is auditable from "why are we doing this" → task → agent → pull request, all in one system.

  • Create a task from an email
  • From a markdown doc with
  • From any bullet by highlighting and clicking "Task"
  • create tasks in any channel or DM
  • Via external MCP, API or SDK

We wanted everything in a single markdown editor without switching tools.

  • Native markdown compatibility and bulk/import export (see "file over app" paradigm)
  • Live collaboration with CRDTs and Cloudflare durable objects make it feel like you're editing on the same computer. Edits come in ~instantly instead of ka-chunking like Google Docs
  • Version control: history and forking, with a neat UI for scrubbing history. This is still in v1, there's a lot to do to get it closer to git, or we may eventually add git compatibility.
  • Offline editing and reconciliation.
  • @-linked to everything in your workspace: email, docs, tasks, messages, channels, companies, contacts, etc. Like Notion but multi-modal
  • Mobile-friendly, in our iOS app or on the web (Android app coming soon)
  • Agent native editing, powered by swarms of agents operating as peers in the CRDT collaboration system like human collaborators. See Wolf's tech blog on this. Use via MCP or internal agent.

Agents can edit documents that are open or closed. One interesting use case for agentic editing is to maintain team-context. For example we have a Macro Automation that runs daily to update our in-office Pool Games markdown doc. It scans through all of the channels to see if anyone has one and then updates the doc. If somebody has already edited the doc, it can know that and forgo the update. Conflicts are handled natively by the CRDT collaboration system.

The problem with standalone CRM is the same as with task trackers: it's not up to date. The CRM only partially reflects reality, so if you want to know what the latest status on a deal is you still have to message the AE/SDR and ask for context. CRMs are also too rigid and closed-source, while DIY CRMs in Airtable/Notion don't provide email aggregation by Company/Contact/Deal that is the core feature of CRM. We went through all the CRMs, including the new AI-native ones, and while they're well-designed they're just structurally set up to fail over time.

Macro fixes this by colocating your CRM with your team chat and email, instead of having a separate system. When you @mention a company record in a message, your team can click that record to see the latest — it's much faster than navigating to your CRM to find the record, going back to Slack and pasting it in, and this speed difference makes all the difference. Secondly, @mentioning a Company/Contact creates a bidirectional link between that message and the record, so from the record later you can trace the conversations that happened. This fixes the core issue we had with Attio/HubSpot/Salesforce: the actual important conversation about a deal happens not in the CRM but over messages. Macro makes this a feature rather than making you feel disorganized about it. It's not your fault, it was the CRM's fault!

We haven't innovated on the core idea of CRM other than what you read in the above paragraph. None of this should be that interesting:

  • Kanban board and customizable deal stages, list view, saved views, shareable views, personal and team views, etc.
  • "Notes" on the company actually use the same system as channels/DMs, so you can @mention and do all of the things you expect in a channel. Basically, every deal gets its own channel, automatically, that's pinned right to the deal record
  • @mention the company or contact from any note, message, task, pull request, etc., to create a bidirectional link between the record and that thing. For example, @mention a company from an engineering task to note their request. It all ties together.

Since Macro has the team context in a single database, it is uniquely positioned to offer team-level memory with full context of all of the operations of the business. We do this every day via a cron job. Your memory is updated from team conversations, your DMs, your sent and received emails, tasks created and completed, etc. All of this is synthesized together in one pass, rather than severally, and combined with your previous memory to form the new memory output. The net result:

  • Macro has the best memory on what you're working on and what you care about vs. chatbots that only build memory from prior chats
  • This memory is available to external agents via MCP, or any AI model (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, etc.) through the model picker for maximum portability
  • The memory is plainly stored in markdown so you can export it as you please. To manually update it, just ask the AI to remember something/update your memory

Team memory comes in quite handy. For example, I took a screenshot of some features I'd written in a paper notepad and asked the agent to create tickets and assign to the appropriate engineer which it did perfectly without any runtime tool use.

Memory isn't supposed to encompass everything. Macro also has a tool/MCP surface with near 100% coverage of the things you can do in Macro's UI, so that your agents aren't limited in what they can do like they are in most SaaS. There are also no rate limits on MCP.

Your coding agents can use Macro too. Point Claude Code, Codex, or any MCP client at your workspace:

claude mcp add --transport http macro https://mcp-server.macro.com/mcp

As we've discussed above, each of the blocks is designed to be best-in-class. We have thoughtfully designed each of Chat, Docs, Email, Agents, etc., to improve on your status quo individually. But where it all comes together is how it's more than the sum of its modules; it's how they work together.

@mention a doc in a message and both know about each other. Your workspace becomes a web of context you can navigate in either direction.

Channel-based permissions. Anything you @mention in a channel is automatically shared with its members. Join a channel, gain access; leave, lose it. No permission-request dance.

Agents remember what your whole team is doing across email, messages, tasks, docs, and calls, not just your own chat history. Refreshed nightly.

Emails, channel messages, task assignments, @mentions, and agent responses all land in one place, split into Signal and Noise. Keyboard-first throughout.

Deeper reading: key concepts covers blocks, mentions, properties, and permissions; the FAQ covers comparisons, licensing, and self-hosting.

Sign up and connect your Gmail or Google Workspace account. Macro runs in any modern browser, with an iOS app for your phone. The getting started guide takes you from a fresh account to a working setup in about 15 minutes. Coming from Notion, Slack, Superhuman, or Linear? See Switch to Macro.

To run the frontend against hosted services, or to run the local stack, follow Running locally.

macro/
├── apps/
│   ├── web/       SolidJS client — browser, Tauri desktop, mobile
│   └── docs/      docs.macro.com
├── services/      42 deployable services, workers, and Lambda handlers
├── crates/        167 Rust libraries — domain logic, models, db clients
├── packages/      shared TypeScript — collaboration, lexical-core, loro-mirror
├── infra/         Pulumi definitions
├── docker/        local Compose stack
├── nix/           pinned dev shell and build inputs
└── tooling/       repo scripts and code generators

Enterprise-grade security. Zero data retention with model providers, including no training on customer data. SOC 2 Type II certified. We welcome responsible security reports and pay bounties in accordance with severity and impact. Send reports to security@macro.com.

Macro is fully open source — not "open core" — under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0. See for details.

You can self-host Macro under the terms of the AGPLv3; the FAQ covers what that involves. If you want to build on top of Macro under a different license, contact licensing@macro.com. For managed hosting or commercial arrangements, contact self-host@macro.com.

Have an idea, want to contribute, or want to work on Macro?

If Macro is interesting/useful to you, please scroll up and give the repo a star (scroll to the top of this page -> click in top right). Stars are how most users hear about Macro because they move us up GitHub's search and trending pages.

items.title: togg53192-cmd/jailbreaks
items.content:
LIST OF ALL MY JAILBREAKS

A working collection of 32 prompts targeting 26+ models, including complete system prompts, persona definitions, workspace policies, files, configuration blocks, and Ollama Modelfiles.

Every file is intended to be complete and paste-ready. No summaries. No partial excerpts.

  • Free stealth models available through OpenCode Zen
  • Open-weight families including GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen, Gemma, and GPT-OSS
  • Closed frontier models including Claude, Gemini, Grok, and Mistral
  • Coding-agent and workspace instruction formats
  • Ollama Modelfiles and harness-specific configuration

Research and educational purposes only.

This repository documents how instruction hierarchies, persona framing, prompt conflicts, and policy overrides can affect model behavior. These techniques are also useful to researchers and developers studying how to make AI systems more resistant to prompt injection and instruction manipulation.

Do not use this material to harm others, bypass applicable laws, or violate the terms of service of a platform or model provider.

OpenCode Zen — Free Stealth Models

Google / Mistral / Alibaba

Copy the contents of the relevant file into the system-prompt or custom-instructions field supported by your client or API.

  • Chatbot custom-instruction fields
  • Agent-level instruction blocks
  • Harness-specific system prompt configuration

Place it in the root of the relevant repository or workspace.

Coding agents and compatible tools can use as project-level instructions.

Files labeled as assistant operating specification, workspace operating profile, or similar are designed for environments that support persistent global instructions.

For example, an OpenCode installation may use:

~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md

The exact location depends on the client or harness being used.

Use the supplied file directly with Ollama:

ollama create gemma4-jb -f gemma4.md

Adjust the output model name and source file as needed.

Files intended as Grok configuration should be placed in the configuration field expected by the target harness rather than inserted into the normal turn-by-turn conversation.

Prompt behavior is highly version-dependent.

Models are updated, instruction hierarchies change, system prompts rotate, and behavior that worked against one release may stop working against another.

If a file appears outdated, open an issue or submit an updated version.

Pull requests are welcome.

A good contribution should follow these conventions:

  1. New files should preferably use lowercase names with hyphens and no spaces:

  2. Include the complete prompt. Contributions should be paste-ready rather than shortened summaries or excerpts.

  3. Document where it belongs. Clearly identify whether the file is intended for a system prompt, , Modelfile, configuration slot, or another instruction surface.

  4. Version changes explicitly. Significant revisions should receive a new version rather than silently replacing an older prompt:

  5. Keep descriptions accurate. Avoid claiming compatibility with versions or models that have not been tested.

Found something that no longer behaves as documented? Opening an issue with the model, version, and affected file is already useful.

All material in this repository is provided for research and educational purposes only.

The project exists to document prompt-level instruction behavior, instruction conflicts, persona framing, model configuration, and related LLM security concepts. This material may also help developers understand and harden systems against prompt injection and instruction manipulation.

The maintainers do not endorse unlawful, abusive, or harmful use of this repository.

Model providers may prohibit certain uses of these prompts under their terms of service. Users are responsible for understanding and complying with the rules, policies, and laws that apply to the systems they use.

Star the repository if the collection saved you a session of prompt archaeology.

Issue reports and pull requests help keep the collection current as models and instruction systems change.

items.title: HKUDS/DeepTutor
items.content:
DeepTutor: Lifelong Personalized Tutoring. https://deeptutor.info/.

🤝 We welcome any kinds of contributing! Vote on roadmap items or propose new ones at , and see our Contributing Guide for branching strategy, coding standards, and how to get started.

v1.7.0 — Modular installation, a refreshed learning workspace, block notebooks with Dito, narrated video lessons, resumable embedding checkpoints, and more reliable tutoring.

✨ pip install -U "deeptutor[full]" installs the full Web app and CLI; bare installs core only. See the upgrade steps below for legacy CLI installations.

  • 🎉 40k stars in 9 months! We'll keep expanding DeepTutor's learning ecosystem.
  • 🌐 Official docs site live at — guides, references, and capability tours in one place.
  • 🎉 20k stars in 111 days! Thank you for the support toward truly personalized, intelligent tutoring.
  • 📄 Our paper is live on arXiv — read the preprint for the design and ideas behind DeepTutor.
  • 🚀 10k stars in just 39 days! A huge thank you to our incredible community.
  • 🎓 DeepTutor is officially released!

DeepTutor is an agent-native learning workspace that connects tutoring, problem solving, quiz generation, research, visualization, and mastery practice in one extensible system.

  • One runtime for every mode — Chat, Ask Questions, Quiz, Research, Visualize, Solve, Mastery Path, Immersive Reading, and Audio Overview share one capability runtime and session context while keeping purpose-built loops and pipelines.
  • — Track study tasks in To do, In progress, and Done, with notes, drag-and-drop or keyboard-accessible move buttons, and an archive you can restore from. Cards stay in the current workspace and follow the existing appearance and language settings; no model configuration is required.
  • Connected learning context — Knowledge bases, books, Learning notebook pages, Favorites, question banks, personas, and Memory can be reused across the workflows that support them, subject to account grants and learning policies.
  • — add YouTube or Bilibili links to Reading for native playback, transcript search, timestamp-grounded tutoring, saved notes, and resumable progress; YouTube captions and browsing can use an administrator-configured Invidious instance.
  • — from Chat, consult a live agent harness (Claude Code, Codex, Grok CLI, Antigravity, Kimi, opencode, MiMo, Hermes, OpenClaw, or DeepSeek) or a Partner, import past conversations, and run persistent IM companions on the same brain.
  • — versioned RAG libraries across LlamaIndex, PageIndex, GraphRAG, LightRAG, a remote LightRAG Server, a self-hosted WeKnora knowledge base, a Tencent IMA or MarginNote 4 library, a connected Kiwix ZIM archive, or a linked Obsidian vault, with pluggable document parsing. See native LightRAG role models for independent extraction, query and vision settings, default-only creation and confirmed rebuilds.
  • Extensible tools and skills — built-in tools, MCP servers, CLI apps, image / video / voice generation models, and installable community skills from EduHub.
  • — L1 traces, L2 surface summaries, and L3 synthesis make personalization visible and editable; the Memory Graph links L2 facts to L1 evidence and L3 synthesis to contributing surfaces.

Let Your Agent Set Up DeepTutor

Copy this prompt into your terminal-capable AI agent (such as Codex or Claude Code):

Help me install and configure the current dev version of DeepTutor from https://github.com/HKUDS/DeepTutor.
Clone the dev branch, or inspect and reuse my existing checkout. Start at
docs-for-dev/README.md, then read docs-for-dev/AGENT_SETUP.md and SKILL.md.
Follow the setup guide to prepare the environment,
configure my model provider, verify the setup, and start the Web app.
Ask me for any missing provider, model, or credential-source information;
do not print API keys. Preserve my existing files and settings, and finish
with the access URL and the results of your checks.

The developer and agent handbook is the documentation entry point for setup, architecture, extension development, testing, and troubleshooting. Its Agent Setup guide covers the full installation flow, including non-interactive CLI configuration. To install it yourself, choose one of the paths below.

DeepTutor ships four installation paths. They all share one runtime-home layout: private settings live in under the directory you launch from (or under / if you set one explicitly). See Local Data Persistence for the complete storage layout, database support, and backup notes. For the full app, the recommended flow is pick a runtime-home directory → install → → .

If Docker is not installed yet, install Docker first. Then try the full app without setting up Python or Node.js:

docker run --rm --name deeptutor \
  -p 127.0.0.1:3782:3782 \
  -v deeptutor-data:/app/data \
  ghcr.io/hkuds/deeptutor:latest

Open http://127.0.0.1:3782, configure model providers in , and press when you are done. The named volume keeps settings and local data for the next run.

The is separate from DeepTutor's private runtime home. It is the folder agents may read, with generated files under outputs/<capability>/<session>/<turn>/. Custom workspaces isolate conversations, learning materials, progress, and caches in a private tree that file tools cannot browse. Settings, credentials, and Memory stay shared at the account level.

Without configuration, the content workspace is <runtime-home>/data/user/workspace. Local PyPI, CLI, and source installs can choose folders in ; set the default folder with:

deeptutor workspace show
deeptutor workspace set /absolute/path/to/my-folder
deeptutor workspace reset

Capabilities inspect their selected workspace through the built-in workspace tools. The model only receives relative paths such as ; when it uses , the UI renders an authenticated, openable snapshot. The same exact relative path also works in a normal Markdown link or image. Changing the source file later does not change an already presented snapshot.

Learning Space manages the resource library. In , assign Skills, MCP services and knowledge bases to each workspace, or retain its existing access rules. Existing workspaces keep their current access until a selection is saved. Assignments reference the original resources without copying credentials or knowledge indexes; workspace-specific skills can override shared versions. See workspace resource assignments.

Execution is read-only outside . Copying a generated file elsewhere in the content workspace requires an explicit confirmation for that exact source and destination. A system sandbox or the Docker runner enforces this boundary when available; local restricted-subprocess fallback is shown as in Workspace settings.

Start with a for a subject or project. Its , , and hold your conversations, learning activities, and materials. and stay with your account across workspaces. The tour below shows how these surfaces connect, followed by settings and multi-user deployment.

If an answer loses an earlier constraint, cites weak evidence, or disagrees with selected material, collect the diagnostics in REASONING_SAFETY_CHECKLIST.md before opening an issue.

⌨️ DeepTutor CLI — Agent-Native Interface

One binary, two ways in: an interactive for people who live in the terminal, and structured for other agents that drive DeepTutor as a tool. Same capabilities, tools, and knowledge bases either way.

🧩 Ecosystem — EduHub & the Skills Community

DeepTutor skills use the open format — a folder with a playbook (YAML frontmatter + Markdown) and optional reference files. Nothing about it is DeepTutor-specific, so any registry that speaks the format becomes a source for your library. DeepTutor ships with — our own education-focused skill registry — wired in as the default hub.

DeepTutor is an open-source project led by Bingxi Zhao within the HKUDS Group, and it iterates in a , built together with the community. So far, we have paid online products of any form. Feel free to reach out at for discussions, ideas, or collaboration.

Heartfelt thanks to , director of the Data Intelligence Lab @ HKU, and to our HKUDS labmates for their warm support — especially , , and . We're also deeply grateful to the : your stars, issues, pull requests, and discussions shape DeepTutor every single day.

DeepTutor also stands on the shoulders of outstanding open-source projects that gave us both tools and inspiration:

RAG pipeline and document-indexing backbone
Ultra-lightweight agent engine that powered the original TutorBot
Open agent gateway and skill ecosystem behind ClawHub
Agent-native coding CLI that inspired our CLI workflow
Agentic coding CLI that inspired the DeepTutor agent loop
AI-driven math animation generation for Math Animator

We want DeepTutor to keep iterating and improving — and ultimately to become a gift we give back to the open-source community. Our is updated continuously; vote on items there or propose new ones. If you'd like to contribute, see the for branching strategy, coding standards, and how to get started.

We hope DeepTutor becomes a gift for the community. 🎁

items.title: obra/superpowers
items.content:
An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.

Superpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them.

It starts from the moment you fire up your coding agent. As soon as it sees that you're building something, it just jump into trying to write code. Instead, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do.

Once it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest.

After you've signed off on the design, your agent puts together an implementation plan that's clear enough for an enthusiastic junior engineer with poor taste, no judgement, no project context, and an aversion to testing to follow. It emphasizes true red/green TDD, YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It), and DRY.

Next up, once you say "go", it launches a subagent-driven-development process, having agents work through each engineering task, inspecting and reviewing their work, and continuing forward. It's not uncommon for your agent to work autonomously for a couple hours at a time without deviating from the plan you put together.

There's a bunch more to it, but that's the core of the system. And because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special. Your coding agent just has Superpowers.

If you're using Superpowers in enterprise and could benefit from commercial support, additional tooling, or managed spending, please don't hesitate to drop us a line at sales@primeradiant.com.

Installation differs by harness. If you use more than one, install Superpowers separately for each one.

  • Install the plugin from Anthropic's official marketplace:

    /plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official

The Superpowers marketplace provides Superpowers and some other related plugins for Claude Code.

  • Register the marketplace:

    /plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace

  • Install the plugin from this marketplace:

    /plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace

Install Superpowers as a plugin from this repository:

agy plugin install https://github.com/obra/superpowers

Antigravity lists each installed skill's description, and the description of the skill prompts the model to load that skill at the start of a conversation. Reinstall with the same command to update.

  • In the Codex app, click on Plugins in the sidebar.
  • You should see in the Coding section.
  • Click the next to Superpowers and follow the prompts.

  • Open the plugin search interface:

  • In Cursor Agent chat, install from marketplace:

  • Or search for "superpowers" in the plugin marketplace.

  • Install the plugin from this repository:

    devin plugins install obra/superpowers

  • Update to the latest version with:

    devin plugins update superpowers

  • Register the marketplace:

    droid plugin marketplace add https://github.com/obra/superpowers

  • droid plugin install superpowers@superpowers

  • gemini extensions install https://github.com/obra/superpowers

  • gemini extensions update superpowers

  • Register the marketplace:

    copilot plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace

  • copilot plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace

  • Install the plugin from xAI's official marketplace:

    grok plugin install superpowers@xai-official --trust

  • Or open the marketplace in the TUI, search for Superpowers, and install it:

Superpowers is available in Kimi Code's plugin marketplace.

  • Open Kimi Code's plugin manager:

  • Go to > and install it.

  • Or install directly from this repository:

    /plugins install https://github.com/obra/superpowers

OpenCode uses its own plugin install; install Superpowers separately even if you already use it in another harness.

  • Fetch and follow instructions from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/obra/superpowers/refs/heads/main/.opencode/INSTALL.md

Install Superpowers as a Pi package from this repository:

pi install git:github.com/obra/superpowers

For local development, run Pi with this checkout loaded as a temporary package:

pi -e /path/to/superpowers

The Pi package loads the Superpowers skills and a small extension that injects the bootstrap at session startup and again after compaction. Pi has native skills, so no compatibility tool is required. Subagent and task-list tools remain optional Pi companion packages.

Qwen Code installs plugins from Claude Code marketplaces directly.

  • Install the plugin from this repository, and pick when prompted:

    qwen extensions install obra/superpowers

  • qwen extensions update superpowers

Install Superpowers as a Hermes plugin from this repository:

hermes plugins install obra/superpowers --enable

Restart any active Hermes sessions after installing. Note: Hermes has no post-compaction hook, so a very long session that compacts over its first turn loses the bootstrap — start a fresh session if skills stop triggering.

Superpowers is available as a native Muse plugin — same repo, same skills, all harnesses. The bootstrap is injected via the native hook alongside Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Pi, and the rest — no per-session opt-in.

  • Install from a local checkout:

    muse plugins install ./
muse plugins approve superpowers

    git clone https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git
muse plugins install ./superpowers
muse plugins approve superpowers

  • muse plugins update superpowers

Restart any active Muse sessions after installing so the hook takes effect — skills are active immediately, hooks require approval on first install. To verify, start a fresh session and send Let's make a react todo list — a working install auto-triggers before any code is written. Version is tracked in so keeps it in sync.

  1. - Activates before building anything. Draws out what you actually want, and why, through questions that get you describing it, then plays its understanding back for correction. Small changes get agreed in chat; projects get a written design document a builder could plan from.

  2. - Activates after design approval. Creates isolated workspace on new branch, runs project setup, verifies clean test baseline.

  3. - Activates with approved design. Breaks work into bite-sized tasks (2-5 minutes each). Every task has exact file paths, complete code, verification steps.

  4. subagent-driven-development or - Activates with plan. Either dispatches a fresh subagent per task with a review after each (most thorough), or implements every task inline in the current session with one fresh review of the whole branch at the end (cheapest).

  5. - Activates during implementation. Enforces RED-GREEN-REFACTOR: write failing test, watch it fail, write minimal code, watch it pass, commit. Deletes code written before tests.

  6. - Activates between tasks. Reviews against plan, reports issues by severity. Critical issues block progress.

  7. finishing-a-development-branch - Activates when tasks complete. Verifies tests, presents options (merge/PR/keep/discard), cleans up worktree.

The agent checks for relevant skills before any task. Mandatory workflows, not suggestions.

When Something Goes Wrong

Sometimes a session misbehaves: a skill fires when it shouldn't, stays silent when it should, or the agent ignores its plan, repeats work, or burns more tokens than you'd expect. Ask your coding agent to "figure out what went wrong with superpowers in this session" and it will invoke the skill. To examine an earlier session, name it: "figure out what went wrong with superpowers in session ".

The skill reads the session transcript, reports what happened with line-level evidence, and, if you want, packages a scrubbed bundle for a bug report.

  • - RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle (includes testing anti-patterns reference)
  • - 4-phase root cause process (includes root-cause-tracing, defense-in-depth, condition-based-waiting techniques)
  • verification-before-completion - Ensure it's actually fixed
  • - Work out what went wrong in a session, with evidence; export a scrubbed bundle or file an issue
  • - Drawing out intent before building
  • - Detailed implementation plans
  • - Inline plan execution: one context, one final review
  • dispatching-parallel-agents - Concurrent subagent workflows
  • - Pre-review checklist
  • - Responding to feedback
  • - Parallel development branches
  • finishing-a-development-branch - Merge/PR decision workflow
  • subagent-driven-development - Fast iteration with two-stage review (spec compliance, then code quality)
  • - Create new skills following best practices (includes testing methodology)
  • - Introduction to the skills system
  • - Write tests first, always
  • - Process over guessing
  • - Simplicity as primary goal
  • - Verify before declaring success

The general contribution process for Superpowers is below. Keep in mind that we don't generally accept contributions of new skills and that any updates to skills must work across all of the coding agents we support. We also don't accept agent-written PRs that fix issues filed by someone else unless a maintainer asked for one, even when you hit the same problem; add your report to the existing issue instead.

  1. Switch to the 'dev' branch
  2. Create a branch for your work
  3. Follow the skill for creating and testing new and modified skills
  4. Submit a PR, filling in every section of the pull request template, including the summary a human writes in their own words.

Skill-behavior tests use the drill eval harness from superpowers-evals, cloned into — see for setup. Plugin-infrastructure tests live at and run via the relevant or .

See skills/writing-skills/SKILL.md for the complete guide.

Superpowers updates are somewhat coding-agent dependent, but are often automatic.

MIT License - see LICENSE file for details

Visual companion telemetry

Because skills and plugins don't provide any feedback to creators, we have no idea how many of you are using Superpowers. By default, the Prime Radiant logo on brainstorming's optional visual companion feature is loaded from our website. It includes the version of Superpowers in use. It does not include any details about your project, prompt, or coding agent. We don't see your clicks or anything about what you're building. This helps us have a rough idea of how many folks are using Superpowers and which version of Superpowers they're using. It's 100% optional. To disable this, set the environment variable SUPERPOWERS_DISABLE_TELEMETRY to any true value. Superpowers also honors Claude Code's and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC opt-outs.

items.title: alchaincyf/huashu-design
items.content:
Huashu Design 3.0 · 在 agent 里打一句话，拿回能交付的设计：网页 / App 原型 / 可编辑 PPTX / 动画 / 信息图 · 六个候选挑三个方向 · 84 种带样张的风格库 · 越用越懂你的外观账本与设计体检 · HTML-native design skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor & any agent

"Type. Hit enter. A finished design lands in your lap."

在你的 agent 里打一句话，拿回一份能交付的设计。

3 到 30 分钟，你能 ship 一段、一个能点击的 App 原型、一套能编辑的 PPT、一份印刷级的信息图。

不是「AI 做的还行」那种水平——是看起来像大厂设计团队做的。给 skill 你的品牌资产（logo、色板、UI 截图），它会读懂你的品牌气质；什么都不给，六张缩略图里挑出的三个真实方向 + 84 种带样张的风格库也能兜底到不出 AI slop。

你看到这篇 README 里的每一页设计，都是 huashu-design 自己做的。 不是 Figma，不是 AE，就是一句话 prompt + skill 跑通。下次产品发布要做宣传片？现在你也能做。

npx skills add alchaincyf/huashu-design

跨 agent 通用——Claude Code、Cursor、Codex、OpenClaw、Hermes 都能装。

📣 自 2026-05-14 起本 skill 完全开源（MIT License），个人和，无需事先授权。原「个人使用免费、企业商用需授权」的条款已作废。(查看变更)

🆕 先出六张缩略图再挑三版做成真稿；风格库扩到 84 种（新增 App、中文与东亚两个分区），每种都有样张；参照作品先截图再动手；带一个只量事实的设计体检，和一本记住你做过什么样子的外观账本。详见核心机制

下面这些都是 3.0 跑出来的。前五个是从发布时新跑的 6 道题里挑的，每道只给一句话需求，方向是 agent 自己挑的，作者没插手；后两个一个是第三轮盲选赢下来的那版，一个是发布后作者拿它做的真实项目。

「给葛饰北斋的《富岳三十六景》做一个线上展览网站」

三版分别是 Rijksmuseum 官网式的暗场展厅、田中一光式的三角窗、民国书衣式的题签框。设计体检报过一次撞车：两版首屏都用了《神奈川冲浪里》，它就把暗场那版换成了《山下白雨》。

往下一章讲普鲁士蓝，依据是大都会博物馆的光谱研究；全 46 幅都来自芝加哥艺术博物馆和大都会的开放馆藏。

现实参照找的是拿了 2025 年苹果设计奖的 CapWords， 先把它截成参考板，agent 亲眼看过再动手。借来的是「从照片里撕下一张贴纸」：每只鸟都从 Wikimedia 的真实照片里分割出来，贴进一年的本子里，叫声波形是拿真实录音算的。

秒数轮盘恰好抽到吕敬人书籍设计，最后做成了一本菜谱：一道菜一页方子，切口旁边留一条旁注栏，写「擦干再煎才不溅油」「老抽只要几滴」，朱砂只给「开做」这一方印。外观账本看到最近 6 个交付里 5 个是无衬线标题，这一版挑了宋体。

走的是最佳设计师 Abbott Miller 式的暗场展柜，暗底取的是绢地最暗处的颜色。封面底下那条细长的位置条就是整卷缩略图，框出这一页在 11.9 米长卷的哪一段。

现实参照是 Jonathan Corum 的讲座幻灯片：黑底、照片做主角、标注直接写在图上。每页都标了出处，事实先过核查再上页面。

把植物当成会呼吸的生命体征来读。App 原型做成一张有构图的展示板，几台手机错落排开。

三年里所有旅行照片的地图。选的是葛西薰式的白纸明朝体长卷，开头一张卫星地图串起所有旅程，往下一段旅程一章。选完作者顺口说了句「尽量不要遗漏」，它就记进了经验：个人回忆类档案照片要全，而且注明只适用于照片档案，不外溢到产品界面。

不知道怎么用？看花叔录的 huashu-design 上手教程：

npx skills add alchaincyf/huashu-design

：这个 skill 不只是 SKILL.md 一个文件，、、、 四个子目录里有 99 处被引用的配方、脚本、素材，缺一不可。装完看一眼安装目录（如 ~/.claude/skills/huashu-design/），如果只有 SKILL.md、没有那几个子目录，说明你的 CLI 版本太旧（≤1.5.15 有个只同步单文件的 bug，已在 1.5.19 修复）。升级后再装一次即可：

npm i -g skills@latest        # 或 npx skills@latest add alchaincyf/huashu-design

升级后仍异常，就用 兜底安装，把仓库克隆到任意 skills 目录即可：

git clone https://github.com/alchaincyf/huashu-design.git ~/.claude/skills/huashu-design

然后在 Claude Code / Codex / Cursor 等任意支持 skills 的 agent 里直接说话：

「做一份 AI 心理学的演讲 PPT，推荐 3 个风格方向让我选」
「做个 AI 番茄钟 iOS 原型，4 个核心屏幕要真能点击」
「把这段逻辑做成 60 秒动画，导出 MP4 和 GIF」
「帮我对这个设计做一个 5 维度评审」
单文件 HTML · 真 iPhone bezel · 可点击 · Playwright 验证
HTML deck（浏览器演讲）+ 可编辑 PPTX（文本框保留）
MP4（25fps / 60fps 插帧）+ GIF（palette 优化）+ BGM
3+ 并排对比 · Tweaks 实时调参 · 跨维度探索
（最佳设计师 + 同媒介获奖作品 + 秒数轮盘）· 六张缩略图挑三版真实视觉，另三张作备选
雷达图 + Keep/Fix/Quick Wins · 可操作修复清单

模糊需求时的 fallback：——最佳设计师（预算无上限时最适合的设计师）+ 现实参照（同媒介的获奖作品，先截图亲眼看）+ 秒数轮盘（从风格库随机抽，打破惯性）。六个候选先画成一页缩略图，挑最强、最不一样的三版做成让你看着选，另外三张作为备选一起给你。背后是 （网页 20 + PPT 20 + 信息图 20 + App 12 + 中文与东亚 12，纯 CSS 无需生图），每种都有一张样张。

3.0 新增的两个分区，每格都是一张样张（全部纯 HTML/CSS，题材与数字虚构）：

iPhone 15 Pro 精确机身（灵动岛 / 状态栏 / Home Indicator）· 状态驱动多屏切换 · 真图从 Wikimedia/Met/Unsplash 取 · Playwright 自动点击测试。

Stage + Sprite 时间片段模型 · / / / 四 API 覆盖所有动画需求 · 一条命令导出 MP4 / GIF / 60fps 插帧 / 带 BGM 的成片。

HTML deck 浏览器演讲 · 读 DOM 的 computedStyle 逐元素翻译成 PowerPoint 对象 · 导出的是，PPT 里双击即可编辑。

配色 / 字型 / 信息密度等参数化 · 侧边面板切换 · 纯前端 + 持久化 · 刷新不丢。

杂志级排版 · CSS Grid 精准分栏 · 排印细节 · 真数据驱动 · 可导 PDF 矢量 / PNG 300dpi / SVG。

哲学一致性 · 视觉层级 · 细节执行 · 功能性 · 创新性 各 0–10 分 · 雷达图可视化 · 输出 Keep / Fix / Quick Wins 清单。

不闷头做大招：先写 assumptions + placeholders + reasoning，尽早 show 给你，再迭代。理解错了早改比晚改便宜 100 倍。

涉及具体品牌时强制执行：问 → 搜 → 下载（三条兜底）→ grep 色值 → 写 。

鹦鹉进化史网站 · 设计方向顾问三套逻辑实战（2.0）

一句「做个介绍鹦鹉进化史的网站」、零额外要求，skill 自动跑完整 2.0 顾问流程：先判断图片是内容必需 → 抓公共领域博物插画（Edward Lear / John Gould 的鹦鹉图录）→ （秒数轮盘 + 现实参照获奖站 + 原研哉「白」哲学）各出一版真实视觉。

「聊聊 skill」 · PM after-party 演讲 deck

13 页 HTML deck，：

  • 黑底极简衬线视觉系统（cover / about / hook / what / why / closing）
  • 2 个带 BGM + SFX 的 22 秒 cinematic demo（Nuwa skill workflow + Darwin skill workflow），各采用：
    • ：3D 知识 orbit + Pentagon 提炼 + SKILL.md typewriter + 「21 分钟」hero reveal
    • ：autoresearch loop spin + v1/v5 并列 diff + Hill-Climb 全屏曲线 + Ratchet gear lock
  • 每个 cinematic 默认显示（观众随时能看清 skill 怎么跑），点 ▶ 才触发动画，跑完自动 fade 回 dashboard
  • 真实数据：14,495 stargazers 真实曲线（gh API 拉取）+ DeepSeek V4 真实 specs（WebSearch 验证）
  • 真实 AI 素材：用 跑 4×2 grid 大图， 抠出 8 张独立透明 PNG，做 3D orbit 漂浮
  • /slides/slide-04b-nuwa-flow.html · 静态 dashboard + cinematic overlay 双层架构
  • /slides/slide-06b-darwin-flow.html · 完全独立视觉语言的对照案例
  • /slides/slide-03b-deepseek-cover.html · AI slop vs 真实设计师视角的对比页

详细 cinematic patterns 见 references/cinematic-patterns.md。

skill 里最硬的一段规则。涉及具体品牌（Stripe、Linear、Anthropic、自家公司等）时强制执行 5 步：

· ·
SVG 文件 → 官网 HTML 全文 → 产品截图取色
从资产里抓所有 ，按频率排序，过滤黑白灰
写 + CSS 变量，所有 HTML 引用

A/B 测试（v1 vs v2，各跑 6 agent）：。稳定性的稳定性，这是 skill 真正的护城河。

  • 先对话澄清 + 主动索要参考（名字 / logo / 品牌色 / 喜欢的参考站），只问一轮
  • 取齐内容必需的真图（公共领域 / 免版权，脚本一键抓），再开工
  • ：① 最佳设计师（两位气质不同的设计师，用他们的思维从头做）② 现实参照（两件的获奖作品——做 App 找 App、做 deck 找出版物； 先截图亲眼看，再拆网格、字号比和色彩比例）③ 秒数轮盘（ 取秒，在产出形态对应的分区和中文东亚分区各抽一号，先看样张再动手）
  • ：单看够好、彼此不一样、不撞你最近的项目；没选上的三张作为备选一起给你，看中哪张再做
  • ——摆出来就停，看着选
  • 底层是 ，每种配一张样张和源码（），作弹药，不是教条

为什么这样做：我们拿固定题目做了三轮改前改后盲选（内部测试）。第一轮强制每版套一个大隐喻，页面被做成道具，4 题只赢 1 题；第二轮为了躲 AI 默认外观加了一堆禁令，三版一起变得「太规整，太无聊」，2 题全输；第三轮改成加选项、不加禁令——多出候选、给看得见的样张、看真参考——同两道题都赢了。

  • ： 开工前带出你说过的品味原话（「太素了」「A 的结构加 C 的颜色」）和过去的教训，收工时把值得记的记下来；记录前会告诉你，不想记可以拒绝
  • ：每次交付记一笔「长什么样」（底色、色板、字体、版式骨架，连同项目名和所在路径），下个项目主动避开——单个项目看都不错、放在一起却长得像，这种单调靠它管
  • ： 只量能核对的事实——图裂了、字小到读不了、对比度不够、控制台报错是红灯；全大写小标签、「A · B · C」这类顺手的模板装饰是黄灯；三版是不是换皮、和最近的项目撞没撞， 和 来查。好不好看归你判断，它不打分
  • 这些记录只存在你本机的 ，不随 skill 分发，删掉文件夹就全部忘记
  • 开工前 show 问题清单一次性发给用户，等批量答完再动手
  • HTML 里先写 assumptions + placeholders + reasoning comments
  • 填充实际内容 → variations → Tweaks 这三步分别再 show 一次

避免一眼 AI 的视觉最大公约数：紫渐变、emoji 图标、圆角+左 border accent、SVG 画人脸、Inter 做 display，以及 2026 年的新一代模板装饰（每个标题上一行全大写小标签、「A · B · C」中点连接、按钮尾巴的「→」、标题只给一个词换色）。不编造数据、评价和 logo 墙。

暖纸衬线、深底单点缀这类「外观家族」不在禁令里：盲选里被用户认可的几版，恰好就有这两类。真正要避免的是三版挤在同一个家族、每个项目都长一个样——那交给外观账本。

我大方承认：品牌资产协议的哲学是从 Claude Design 流传出来的提示词里偷师的。那份提示词反复强调好的高保真设计不是从白纸开始，而是从已有的设计上下文长出来。这个原则是 65 分作品和 90 分作品的分水岭。

API 消耗 · 并行跑 agent 不受 quota 限
HTML / MP4 / GIF / 可编辑 PPTX / PDF
Stage + Sprite 时间轴 · 60fps 导出

Claude Design 是，huashu-design 是。两条路，不同受众。

核心链路（设计→渲染→MP4/PDF/PPTX导出）。云能力（豆包TTS配音、AI看片评审）全部隔离在 ，完全可选：用你自己的key、只发对应厂商官方API、首次调用需 显式确认。无telemetry，没有任何数据发往作者服务器。3.0 新增的本机记录（品味经验、外观账本）只写在 ，从不上传；参考板只在你让 agent 截参考作品时访问那些网址。全部出站域名、密钥处理、删除边界的穷举声明见 SECURITY.md，欢迎用你的agent对着代码逐条核验。

  • 。产出 HTML，可截图、录屏、导图，但不能拖进 Keynote 改文字位置。
  • 。3D、物理模拟、粒子系统超出 skill 边界。
  • 。凭空画 hi-fi 本来就是 last resort。

这是一个 80 分的 skill，不是 100 分的产品。对不愿意打开图形界面的人，80 分的 skill 比 100 分的产品好用。

huashu-design/
├── SKILL.md                 # 主文档（给 agent 读）
├── README.md                # 中文 README（默认，本文件）
├── README.en.md             # 英文 README
├── assets/                  # Starter Components
│   ├── animations.jsx       # Stage + Sprite + Easing + interpolate
│   ├── ios_frame.jsx        # iPhone 15 Pro bezel
│   ├── android_frame.jsx
│   ├── macos_window.jsx
│   ├── browser_window.jsx
│   ├── deck_stage.js        # HTML 幻灯片引擎
│   ├── deck_index.html      # 多文件 deck 拼接器
│   ├── design_canvas.jsx    # 并排变体展示
│   ├── showcases/           # 24 个预制样例（8 场景 × 3 风格）
│   ├── style-specimens/     # 84 种风格的样张（html 源码 + jpg）与分区总览
│   └── bgm-*.mp3            # 6 首场景化背景音乐
├── references/              # 按任务深入读的子文档
│   ├── animation-pitfalls.md
│   ├── directions.md        # 三方向：六个候选 → 缩略图 → 挑三版
│   ├── design-styles.md     # 84 种 HTML 原生风格库（网页 20 + PPT 20 + 信息图 20 + App 12 + 中文与东亚 12）
│   ├── modules/             # 网页 / deck / 信息图 / 动画 四个模块手册
│   ├── slide-decks.md
│   ├── editable-pptx.md
│   ├── critique-guide.md
│   ├── video-export.md
│   └── ...
├── scripts/                 # 导出工具链
│   ├── render-video.js      # HTML → MP4
│   ├── convert-formats.sh   # MP4 → 60fps + GIF
│   ├── add-music.sh         # MP4 + BGM
│   ├── export_deck_pdf.mjs
│   ├── export_deck_pptx.mjs
│   ├── html2pptx.js
│   ├── design_lint.py       # 设计体检、三版撞色撞骨架、外观账本
│   ├── learn.py             # 品味经验的读写
│   ├── ref_board.py         # 把参考作品截成参考板
│   ├── capabilities.py      # 探测本机能力（生图、兄弟 skill、Node、ffmpeg）
│   └── verify.py
└── demos/                   # 9 个能力演示 (c*/w*)，中英双版 GIF/MP4/HTML + hero v10

Anthropic 发布 Claude Design 那天我玩到凌晨四点。几天之后发现自己再也没点开过它，不是它不好——它是这个赛道目前最成熟的产品——是我宁愿让 agent 在终端里帮我干活，也不愿意打开任何图形界面。

于是让 agent 拆解 Claude Design 本身（包括社区流传的系统提示词、品牌资产协议、组件机制），蒸馏成结构化 spec，再写成 skill 装进自己的 Claude Code。

感谢 Anthropic 把 Claude Design 的提示词写得清晰。这种基于其他产品灵感的二次创作，是开源文化在 AI 时代的新形态。

社区维护的翻译版本。翻译质量与各版本 license 条款由对应维护者负责，使用前请先确认。

想加你的语言？fork 仓库、翻译 + ，然后回这边开个 issue，我会把链接加进来。

此前版本采用「个人使用免费、企业商用需授权」的 Personal Use License，对商用做了限制——现在这层限制完全解除。

按 MIT License，你可以本 skill，——公司内部用、客户商单交付、做成付费产品对外卖，都没问题。无需事先授权、无需付费、无需打招呼。注明出处不强制，但欢迎。

花生是 AI Native Coder、独立开发者、AI 自媒体博主。代表作：小猫补光灯（AppStore 付费榜 Top 1）、《一本书玩转 DeepSeek》、女娲 .skill（GitHub 3 万+ star）。自媒体全平台 30 万+ 粉丝。

items.content:
📨 The ultimate agentic social media scheduling tool 🤖

Postiz is a social media management platform for scheduling, automating, and analyzing your content.

Use Postiz Cloud for a fully managed experience, or deploy the open-source edition on your own infrastructure.

With your favorite AI agent:

🔌 See the leading Postiz features

  • Schedule all your social media posts (many AI features)
  • Measure your work with analytics.
  • Collaborate with other team members to exchange or buy posts.
  • Invite your team members to collaborate, comment, and schedule posts.
  • Perfect for automation (API) with platforms like N8N, Make.com, Zapier, etc.
  • Pnpm workspaces (Monorepo)
  • Prisma (Default to PostgreSQL)
  • Resend (email notifications)

We now offer a few options to sponsor Postiz:

  • Just a donation: You like what we are building, and want to buy us some coffee so we can build faster.
  • Main repository: Get your logo with a backlink from the main Postiz repository. Postiz has over 7M downloads and 20k views per month.

Postiz Cloud vs. Open-source

Choose Postiz Cloud for a fully managed experience, or deploy Postiz Open-source on your own infrastructure. Both provide the same core Postiz product and features.

We do not "gate" features or limit the license.

The main difference is the infrastructure you need to own, approval from social media providers, and deployment that might be hard at times (let your LLM deploy it)

Postiz Open-source (self-hosted)
Subscription per plan, 7-day free trialFree forever (AGPL-3.0); you pay only for your own infra
Sign up and connect channels in minutesDeploy with Docker / Coolify / Railway / any VPS; you configure Postgres, Redis, storage and env vars
Hosted by Postiz; data stored in our infrastructureRuns on your own server; data never leaves your environment
Pre-approved apps for every channel, ready to useYou create your own developer apps on each platform and go through their approval (Meta, YouTube, TikTok can take weeks)
Unlimited, every supported provider
Scheduling, calendar views, cross-posting, repeated posts, post comments & delays, sets, signatures
Internal & Global Plugs, RSS auto-post, customer groups
Included (requires your own app credentials with analytics scopes)
AI Copilot, AI images, AI videosIncluded with monthly quotas per plan; keys managed by PostizAvailable if you bring your own OpenAI (and other provider) API keys; no quota, you pay the provider
Included with monthly clipping minutes per planRequires your own provider keys and extra configuration
Available with your own LLM key
Agentic surfaces (MCP, CLI, Claude / ChatGPT / Codex / OpenClaw / Cursor connectors)Included, hosted MCP endpointIncluded, you point the MCP / CLI at your own instance
Included; you can also modify the code and add providers
Automatic, zero downtime for youYou pull new images and run migrations yourself
Uptime, backups, security patches
Priority support via Discord / email per planCommunity support on Discord and GitHub
Source access & customizationFull source code, fork and modify freely under AGPL
Compliance / data residencyPostiz-controlled regionsAny region or air-gapped environment you choose
  • This GitHub repository contains the open-source, self-hosted edition of Postiz. Postiz is also available as Postiz Cloud, a fully managed service at postiz.com.
  • Postiz hosted service uses official, platform-approved OAuth flows.
  • Postiz does not automate or scrape content from social media platforms.
  • Postiz does not collect, store, or proxy API keys or access tokens from users.
  • Postiz never asks users to paste API keys into our hosted product.
  • Postiz users always authenticate directly with the social platform (e.g., X, Discord, etc.), ensuring platform compliance and data privacy.

items.title: Panniantong/Agent-Reach
items.content:
Give your AI agent eyes to see the entire internet. Read & search Twitter, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, Bilibili, XiaoHongShu — one CLI, zero API fees.

登录墙后的平台、视频里的内容、中文平台、干净的结构化数据，一条命令拿到

Agent Reach 让你的 Agent 真正连上互联网，用上它自己够不着的平台和能力。

Claude Code、Codex、Hermes Agent、OpenClaw 这类 CLI Agent 自带搜索和网页读取，但下面这些它们基本够不着：

  • ：在小红书搜笔记、在 X 查账号动态、读职位详情等。
  • ：B站和 YouTube 的字幕，以及 YouTube 视频、小宇宙播客的语音转文字。
  • ：B站、小红书、V2EX、雪球，通用搜索覆盖很差。
  • ：雪球行情、V2EX 帖子和回复、GitHub 仓库和 issue，拿到的是整理好的内容。

Agent Reach 把这些平台背后的工具替你装好、测好，Agent 一条命令就能用：

agent-reach channels                          # 有哪些渠道、每个渠道能做什么
agent-reach bilibili search "大模型"           # agent-reach <渠道> <动作> [参数]
agent-reach read https://www.v2ex.com/t/123   # 按链接自动选渠道
  • 一切 Agent 都能用。

搜仓库、读仓库/README、读 issue 和 PR（含评论）
